Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A)，B)，C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Pasta is no longer off the menu, after a new review of studies suggested that the carbohydrate can form part of a healthy diet, and even help people lose weight. For years, nutritionists have recommended that pasta be kept to a 26 , to cut calories, prevent fat build-up and stop blood sugar 27 up.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项新的研究回顾表明，碳水化合物可以成为健康饮食的一部分，甚至可以帮助人们减肥，因此意大利面不再出现在菜单上。多年来，营养学家一直建议尽量少吃面食，以减少热量、防止脂肪堆积并阻止血糖升高。

paragraphs.sourceText: The low-carbohydrate food movement gave birth to such diets as the Atkins, Paleo and Keto, which advised swapping foods like bread, pasta and potatoes for vegetables, fish and meat. More recently the trend of swapping spaghetti for vegetables has been 28 by clean-eating experts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 低碳水化合物食物运动催生了阿特金斯饮食法、古饮食法和生酮饮食法等饮食法，这些饮食法建议用蔬菜、鱼和肉代替面包、面食和土豆等食物。最近，清洁饮食专家倡导用蔬菜代替意大利面的趋势。

paragraphs.sourceText: But now a 29 review and analysis of 30 studies by Canadian researchers found that not only does pasta not cause weight gain, but three meals a week can help people drop more than half a kilogram over four months. The reviewers found that pasta had been unfairly demonized (妖魔化) because it had been 30 in with other, more fat-promoting carbohydrates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但现在加拿大研究人员对30项研究进行系统回顾和分析发现，面食不仅不会导致体重增加，而且每周三餐可以帮助人们在四个月内减掉半公斤以上。评论者发现，面食被不公平地妖魔化，因为它与其他更容易促进脂肪的碳水化合物混在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: “The study found that pasta didn’t 31 to weight gain or increase in body fat,” said lead author Dr John Sievenpiper. “In 32 the evidence, we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an 33 effect on body weigh outcomes when it is consumed as part of a healthy dietary pattern.” In fact, analysis actually showed a small weigh loss. So 34 to concerns, perhaps pasta can be part of a healthy diet
paragraphs.translationZh: “研究发现面食不会导致体重增加或体内脂肪增加，”主要作者约翰·西文派珀博士说。 “在权衡证据后，我们现在可以有信心地说，当面食作为健康饮食模式的一部分食用时，不会对体重产生不利影响。”事实上，分析显示体重略有减轻。因此，与担忧相反，面食也许可以成为健康饮食的一部分

paragraphs.sourceText: Those involved in the 35 trials on average ate 3.3 servings of pasta a week instead of other carbohydrates, one serving equaling around half a cup. They lost around half a kilogram over an average follow-up of 12 weeks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 参与临床试验的受试者平均每周吃 3.3 份意大利面，而不是其他碳水化合物，一份大约相当于半杯。在平均 12 周的随访中，他们体重减轻了约半公斤。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Best Retailers Combine Bricks and Clicks
paragraphs.translationZh: 最好的零售商将实体和点击相结合

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Retail profits are falling sharply. Stores are closing. Malls are emptying. The depressing stories just keep coming. Reading the earnings announcements of large retail stores like Macy’s, Nordstorm, and Target is about as uplifting as a tour of an intensive care unit. The interact is apparently taking down yet another industry. Brick and mortar stores (实体店) seem to be going the way of the yellow pages. Sure enough, the Census Bureau just released data showing that online retail sales surged 15.2 percent between the first quarter of 2015 and the first quarter of 2016.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）零售利润急剧下降。商店正在关门。商场都空了。令人沮丧的故事不断出现。阅读梅西百货、Nordstorm 和 Target 等大型零售商店的盈利公告就像参观重症监护室一样令人振奋。这种互动显然正在摧毁另一个行业。实体店似乎正在走黄页的道路。果不其然，美国人口普查局刚刚发布的数据显示，2015年第一季度至2016年第一季度网络零售额猛增15.2%。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But before you dump all of your retail stocks, there are more facts you should consider. Looking only at that
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但在抛售所有零售股票之前，您应该考虑更多事实。只看那个

paragraphs.sourceText: 15.2 percent "surge" would be misleading. It was an increase that was on a small base of 6.9 percent. Even when a tiny number grows by a large percentage terms, it is often still tiny.
paragraphs.translationZh: 15.2% 的“激增”可能会产生误导。这一增长的基数较小，仅为 6.9%。即使一个很小的数字以很大的百分比增长，它通常仍然很小。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) More than 20 years after the internet was opened to commerce, the Census Bureau tells us that brick and mortar sales accounted for 92.3 percent of retail sales in the first quarter of 2016. Their data show that only 0.8 percent of retail sales shifted from offline to online between the beginning of 2015 and 2016.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 互联网对商业开放 20 多年后，美国人口普查局告诉我们，2016 年第一季度，实体零售额占零售额的 92.3%。他们的数据显示，2015 年初至 2016 年间，只有 0.8% 的零售额从线下转移到线上。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) So, despite all the talk about drone (无人机) deliveries to your doorstep, all the retail executives expressing anxiety over consumers going online, and even a Presidential candidate exclaiming that Amazon has a "huge antitrust problem," the Census data suggest that physical retail is thriving. Of course, the closed stores, depressed executives, and sinking stocks suggest otherwise. What's the real story?
paragraphs.translationZh: D）因此，尽管人们都在谈论无人机送货上门，所有零售业高管都对消费者上网表示焦虑，甚至总统候选人也感叹亚马逊存在“巨大的反垄断问题”，但人口普查数据表明实体零售业正在蓬勃发展。当然，商店关门、高管情绪低落以及股价下跌表明情况并非如此。真实的故事是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Many firms operating brick and mortar stores are in trouble. The retail industry is getting “reinvented,” as we describe in our new book. Matchmakers. It’s standing in the path of what Schumpeter called a gale (大风) of creative destruction. That storm has been brewing for some time, and as it has reached gale force, most large retailers are searching for a response. As the CFO of Macy’s put it recently, “We’re frankly scratching our heads.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 许多经营实体店的公司都陷入了困境。正如我们在新书中所描述的那样，零售业正在“重塑”。媒人。它正挡住熊彼特所说的创造性破坏的大风。这场风暴已经酝酿了一段时间，随着风暴的强度达到了狂风，大多数大型零售商都在寻求应对措施。正如梅西百货首席财务官最近所说，“坦率地说，我们正在摸不着头脑。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) But it’s not happening as experts predicted. In the peak of the dot. com bubble, brick and mortar retail was one of those industries the internet was going to kill—and quickly. The dot.corn bust discredited most predictions of that sort and in the years that followed, conventional retailers’ confidence in the future increased as Census continued to report weak online sales. And then the gale hit.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 但这并没有像专家预测的那样发生。在点的巅峰。互联网泡沫、实体零售业是互联网将要消灭的行业之一，而且速度很快。 .com 的破产使大多数此类预测都变得不可信，在接下来的几年里，随着人口普查继续报告疲弱的在线销售，传统零售商对未来的信心增强。然后大风袭来。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) It is becoming increasingly clear that retail reinvention isn’t a simple battle to the death between bricks and clicks. It is about devising retail models that work for people who are making increasing use of a growing array of internet-connected tools to change how they search, shop, and buy. Creative retailers are using the new technologies to innovate just about everything stores do from managing inventory, to marketing, to getting paid.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 越来越明显的是，零售业的重塑并不是一场简单的砖块和点击之间的生死之战。它是关于设计适合那些越来越多地使用越来越多的互联网连接工具来改变他们搜索、购物和购买方式的人们的零售模式。创意零售商正在利用新技术对商店所做的几乎所有事情进行创新，从管理库存到营销，再到获得报酬。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) More than drones dropping a new supply of underwear on your doorstep, Apple’s massively successful brick-and-mortar-and-glass retail stores and Amazon’s small steps in the same direction are what should keep old-fashioned retailers awake at night. Not to mention the large number of creative new retailers, like Bonobos, that are blending online and offline experiences in creative ways.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 不仅仅是无人机将新的内衣送到你家门口，苹果巨大成功的实体零售店和亚马逊朝同一方向迈出的小步应该让老式零售商彻夜难眠。更不用说像 Bonobos 这样的大量创意新零售商，他们正在以创造性的方式融合线上和线下体验。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Retail reinvention is not a simple process, and it’s also not happening on what used to be called "Internet Time." Some internet-driven changes have happened quickly, of course. Craigslist quickly overtook newspaper classified ads and turned newspaper economics upside down. But many widely anticipated changes weren’t quick, and some haven’t really started. With the benefit of hindsight (后见之明), it looks like the interact will transform the economy at something like the pace of other great inventions like electricity. B2B commerce, for example, didn’t move mainly online by 2005 as many had predicted in 2000, nor even by 2016, but that doesn’t mean it won’t do so over the next few decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 零售业的重塑并不是一个简单的过程，而且它也不会发生在过去所谓的“互联网时代”。当然，一些互联网驱动的变化发生得很快。 Craigslist 迅速超越了报纸分类广告，并彻底颠覆了报纸经济。但许多广泛预期的变化并不迅速，有些还没有真正开始。事后看来，互动似乎将以电力等其他伟大发明的步伐改变经济。例如，到 2005 年，B2B 商务并没有像许多人在 2000 年预测的那样主要转移到网上，甚至到 2016 年也没有，但这并不意味着它在未来几十年不会这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) But the gale is still blowing. The sudden decline in foot traffic in recent years, even though it hasn’t been accompanied by a massive decline in physical sales, is a critical warning. People can shop more efficiently online and therefore don’t need to go to as many stores to find what they want. There’s a surplus of physical shopping space for the crowds, which is one reason why stores are downsizing and closing.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 但大风仍在吹。近年来人流量的突然下降，尽管并没有伴随着实体销售的大幅下降，但却是一个严重的警告。人们可以更有效地在线购物，因此不需要去那么多商店找到他们想要的东西。人群的实体购物空间过剩，这是商店缩小规模和关闭的原因之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The rise of the mobile phone has recently added a new level of complexity to the process of retail reinvention. Even five years ago most people faced a choice. Sit at your computer, probably at home or at the office, search and browse, and buy. Or head out to the mall, or Main Street, look and shop, and buy. Now, just about everyone has a smartphone, connected to the internet almost everywhere almost all the time. Even when a retailer gets a customer to walk in the store, she can easily see if there’s a better deal online or at another store nearby.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 手机的兴起最近使零售业重塑过程变得更加复杂。即使在五年前，大多数人也面临着选择。坐在电脑前（可能是在家里或办公室），搜索、浏览并购买。或者前往购物中心或主街，参观、购物并购买。现在，几乎每个人都拥有智能手机，几乎随时随地都可以连接到互联网。即使零售商让顾客走进商店，她也可以轻松查看网上或附近的其他商店是否有更好的优惠。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) So far, the main thing many large retailers have done in response to all this is to open online stores, so people will come to them directly rather than to Amazon and its smaller online rivals．Many are having the same problem that newspapers have. Even if they get online traffic, they struggle to make enough money online to compensate for what they are losing offline.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 到目前为止，许多大型零售商针对这一切所做的主要事情就是开设在线商店，这样人们就会直接来到他们那里，而不是亚马逊及其规模较小的在线竞争对手。许多零售商都面临着与报纸相同的问题。即使他们获得了在线流量，他们也很难在网上赚到足够的钱来弥补线下的损失。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) A few seem to be making this work．Among large traditional retailers, Walmart recently reported the best results, leading its stock price to surge, while Macy’s, Target, and Nordstrom’s dropped. Yet Walmart’s year-over-year online sales only grew 7 percent, leading its CEO to lament ( 哀叹), “Growth here is too slow．”Part of the problem is that almost two decades after Amazon filed the one．click patent, the online retail shopping and buying experience is filled with frictions．A recent study graded more than 600 internet retailers on how easy it was for consumers to shop, buy, and pay．Almost half of the sites didn’t get a passing grade and only 18 percent got an A or B．
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 似乎有一些公司正在实现这一目标。在大型传统零售商中，沃尔玛最近公布了最好的业绩，导致其股价飙升，而梅西百货、塔吉特百货和诺德斯特龙百货则下跌。然而，沃尔玛的在线销售额同比仅增长了 7％，导致其首席执行官哀叹：“这里的增长太慢了。”部分问题在于，在亚马逊申请一键点击专利近二十年后，在线零售购物和购买体验充满了摩擦。最近的一项研究对 600 多家互联网零售商进行了消费者购物、购买和支付的容易程度的评级。几乎一半的网站没有获得及格分数，只有 18 家网站没有获得及格分数。百分比得到 A 或 B．

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The turmoil on the ground in physical retail is hard to square with the Census data．Unfortunately, part of the explanation is that the Census retail data are unreliable．Our deep 100k into those data and their preparation revealed serious problems．It seems likely that Census simply misclassifies a large chunk of online sales．It is certain that the Census procedures, which lump the online sales of major traditional retailers like Walmart with“non-store retailers"1ike food trucks．can mask major changes in individual retail categories．The bureau could easily present their data in more useful ways．but they have chosen not to．
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 实体零售业的动荡很难与人口普查数据相符。不幸的是，部分原因是人口普查零售数据不可靠。我们对这些数据进行了 10 万次深入研究，其准备工作揭示了严重的问题。人口普查似乎只是错误地分类了很大一部分在线销售。可以肯定的是，人口普查程序将沃尔玛等主要传统零售商的在线销售与“非商店零售商”1 之类的食品混为一谈。卡车。可以掩盖个别零售类别的重大变化。该局可以轻松地以更有用的方式呈现他们的数据。但他们选择不这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Despite the turmoil, brick and mortar won’t disappear any time soon．The big questions are which, if any, of the large traditional retailers will still be on the scene in a decade or two because they have successfully reinvented themselves, which new players will operate busy stores on Main Streets and maybe even in shopping malls, and how the shopping and buying experience will have changed in each retail category ．Investors shouldn’t write off brick and mortar．Whether they should bet on the traditional players who run those stores now is another matter
paragraphs.translationZh: O）尽管存在动荡，实体店不会很快消失。最大的问题是，哪些大型传统零售商（如果有的话）将在十年或两年内仍然存在，因为它们已经成功地重塑了自己，哪些新参与者将在主要街道甚至购物中心经营繁忙的商店，以及每个零售类别的购物和购买体验将如何改变。投资者不应该贬低实体店。他们是否应该押注于经营这些实体的传统参与者现在商店是另一回事

paragraphs.sourceText: 36.Although online retailing has existed for some twenty years, nearly half of the internet retailers still fail to receive satisfactory feedback from consumers, according to a recent survey．
paragraphs.translationZh: 36.尽管网上零售已经存在了大约二十年，但根据最近的一项调查，近一半的网上零售商仍然未能收到消费者满意的反馈。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37.Innovative retailers integrate internet technologies with conventional retailing to create new retail models．
paragraphs.translationZh: 37.创新零售商将互联网技术与传统零售相结合，创造新的零售模式。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38.Despite what the Census data suggest, the value of physical retail’s stocks has been dropping．
paragraphs.translationZh: 38.尽管人口普查数据表明，实体零售股票的价值一直在下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39.Innovative-driven changes in the retail industry didn’t take place as quickly as widely anticipated．
paragraphs.translationZh: 39.零售业的创新驱动变革并没有像人们普遍预期的那样迅速发生。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Statistics indicate that brick and mortar sales still made up the lion’s share of the retail business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 统计数据表明，实体销售仍占零售业务的最大份额。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Companies that successfully combine online and offline business models may prove to be a big concern for traditional retailers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 成功结合线上和线下商业模式的公司可能会成为传统零售商的一大担忧。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42.Brick and mortar retailers’ faith in their business was strengthened when the dot com bubble burst.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42.当互联网泡沫破灭时，实体零售商对其业务的信心增强了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Despite the tremendous challenges from online retailing, traditional retailing will be here to stay for quite some time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 尽管网上零售面临巨大挑战，但传统零售仍将持续相当长一段时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. With the rise of online commerce, physical retail stores are likely to suffer the same fate as i the yellow pages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 随着在线商务的兴起，实体零售店可能会遭受与黄页相同的命运。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. The wide use of smartphones has made it more complex for traditional retailers to reinvent their business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 智能手机的广泛使用使传统零售商重塑业务变得更加复杂。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Professor Stephen Hawking has warned that the creation of powerful artifcial intelligence (AI) will be “either the best, or the worst thing, ever to happen to humanity”, and praised the creation of an academic institute dedicated to researching the future of intelligence as “ crucial to the future of our civilisation and our species”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 斯蒂芬·霍金教授警告说，强大的人工智能（AI）的诞生将是“人类有史以来发生的最好的事情，也可能是最糟糕的事情”，并赞扬致力于研究智能未来的学术机构的创建“对我们文明和人类物种的未来至关重要”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Hawking was speaking at the opening of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence(LCFI) at Cambridge University, a multi-disciplinary institute that will attempt to tackle some of the open-ended questions raised by the rapid pace of development in AI research. “We spend a great deal of time studying history,” Hawking said, “which, let’s face it, is mostly the history of stupidity. So it’s a welcome change that people are studying instead the future of intelligence.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 霍金在剑桥大学莱弗休姆智能未来中心（LCFI）的开幕式上发表讲话，该中心是一个多学科机构，将试图解决人工智能研究快速发展所带来的一些开放性问题。 “我们花了很多时间研究历史，”霍金说，“让我们面对现实，历史大部分都是愚蠢的历史。因此，人们正在研究智能的未来，这是一个可喜的变化。”

paragraphs.sourceText: While the world-renowned physicist has often been cautious about AI, raising concerns that humanity could be the architect of its own destruction if it creates a super-intelligence with a will of its own, he was also quick to highlight the positives that AI research can bring. “The potential benefits of creating intelligence are huge,” he said. “We cannot predict what we might achieve when our own minds are amplified by AI. Perhaps with the tools of this new technological revolution, we will be able to undo some of the damage done to the natural world by the last one—industrialisation. And surely we will aim to finally eradicate disease and poverty. And every aspect of our lives will be transformed. In short, success in creating AI could be the biggest event in the history of our civilisation.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然这位世界著名物理学家经常对人工智能持谨慎态度，并担心如果人类创造出具有自己意志的超级智能，人类可能会成为自身毁灭的建筑师，但他也很快强调了人工智能研究可以带来的积极影响。 “创造情报的潜在好处是巨大的，”他说。 “当我们的思维被人工智能放大时，我们无法预测我们会取得什么成就。也许借助这场新技术革命的工具，我们将能够消除上一场工业化对自然世界造成的一些损害。当然，我们的目标是最终消除疾病和贫困。我们生活的方方面面都将发生改变。简而言之，成功创造人工智能可能是我们文明史上最重大的事件。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Huw Price, the centre’s academic director and the Bertrand Russell professor of philosophy at Cambridge University, where Hawking is also an academic, said that the centre came about partially as a result of the university’s Centre for Existential Risk. That institute examined a wider range of potential problems for humanity, while the LCFI has a narrow focus.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该中心的学术主任、剑桥大学伯特兰·罗素哲学教授休·普莱斯（霍金也是该大学的一名学者）表示，该中心的成立部分归功于该大学的存在风险中心。该研究所研究了更广泛的人类潜在问题，而 LCFI 的关注范围较窄。

paragraphs.sourceText: AI pioneer Margaret Boden, professor of cognitive science at the University of Sussex, praised the progress of such discussions. As recently as 2009, she said, the topic wasn’t taken seriously, even among AI researchers. “AI is hugely exciting,” she said, “but it has limitations, which present grave dangers given uncritical use.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 人工智能先驱、萨塞克斯大学认知科学教授玛格丽特·博登赞扬了此类讨论的进展。她说，就在 2009 年，这个话题还没有被认真对待，即使是在人工智能研究人员中也是如此。 “人工智能非常令人兴奋，”她说，“但它也有局限性，如果不加批判地使用，就会带来严重的危险。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The academic community is not alone in warning about the potential dangers of AI as well as the potential benefits. A number of pioneers from the technology industry, most famously the entrepreneur Elon Musk, have also expressed their concerns about the damage that a super-intelligent AI could do to humanity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 学术界并不是唯一一个对人工智能的潜在危险和潜在好处发出警告的人。许多科技行业的先驱，其中最著名的是企业家埃隆·马斯克，也表达了他们对超级智能人工智能可能对人类造成的损害的担忧。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The market for products designed specifically for older adults could reach $30 billion by next year, and startups (初创公司) want in on the action. What they sometimes lack is feedback from the people who they hope will use their products. So Brookdale, the country’s largest owner of retirement communities, has been inviting a few select entrepreneurs just to move in for a few days, show off their products and hear what the residents have to say.
paragraphs.translationZh: 到明年，专门为老年人设计的产品市场可能会达到 300 亿美元，初创公司也希望参与其中。他们有时缺乏的是他们希望使用他们产品的人的反馈。因此，美国最大的退休社区所有者布鲁克代尔一直在邀请一些精选的企业家入住几天，展示他们的产品并听取居民的意见。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s what brought Dayle Rodriguez, 28, all the way from England to the dining room of Brookdale South Bay in Torrance, California. Rodriguez is the community and marketing manager for a company called Sentab. The startup’s product, SentabTV, enables older adults who may not be comfortable with computers to access email, video chat and social media using just their televisions and a remote control.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是 28 岁的戴尔·罗德里格斯 (Dayle Rodriguez) 从英国千里迢迢来到加利福尼亚州托伦斯市布鲁克代尔南湾餐厅的原因。 Rodriguez 是 Sentab 公司的社区和营销经理。该初创公司的产品 SentabTV 使那些可能不习惯使用计算机的老年人只需使用电视和遥控器即可访问电子邮件、视频聊天和社交媒体。

paragraphs.sourceText: “It’s nothing new, it’s nothing too complicated and it’s natural because lots of people have TV remotes,”says Rodriguez.
paragraphs.translationZh: “这不是什么新鲜事，也没什么太复杂的，而且很自然，因为很多人都有电视遥控器，”罗德里格斯说。

paragraphs.sourceText: But none of that is the topic of conversation in the Brookdale dining room. Instead, Rodriguez solicits residents’ advice on what he should get on his cheeseburger and how he should spend the afternoon. Playing cards was on the agenda, as well as learning to play mahjong (麻将).
paragraphs.translationZh: 但这些都不是布鲁克代尔餐厅里谈论的话题。相反，罗德里格斯征求居民的建议，告诉他应该在芝士汉堡上加什么以及应该如何度过下午。打牌、学习打麻将都提上了日程。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rodriguez says it’s important that residents here don’t feel like he’s selling them something. “I’ve had more feedback in a passive approach,”he says. “Playing pool, playing cards, having dinner, having lunch,”all work better “than going through a survey of questions. When they get to know me and to trust me, knowing for sure I’m not selling them something—there’ll be more honest feedback from them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 罗德里格斯说，重要的是这里的居民不会觉得他在向他们推销东西。 “我通过被动方式获得了更多反馈，”他说。 “打台球、打牌、吃晚饭、吃午饭，这些都比进行问题调查更有效。当他们了解我并信任我，确定我不会向他们推销东西时，他们就会得到更诚实的反馈。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Rodriguez is just the seventh entrepreneur to move into one of Brookdale’s 1,100 senior living communities. Other new products in the program have included a kind of full-body blow dryer and specially designed clothing that allows people with disabilities to dress and undress themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: Rodriguez 是第七位搬入布鲁克代尔 1,100 个老年生活社区之一的企业家。该计划中的其他新产品包括一种全身吹风机和专门设计的衣服，可以让残疾人自己穿脱衣服。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mary Lou Busch, 93, agreed to try the Sentab system. She tells Rodriguez that it might be good for someone, but not for her.
paragraphs.translationZh: 93 岁的玛丽·卢·布希 (Mary Lou Busch) 同意尝试 Sentab 系统。她告诉罗德里格斯，这可能对某人有好处，但对她不利。

paragraphs.sourceText: “I have the computer and FaceTime, which I talk with my family on,”she explains. She also has an iPad and a smartphone. “So I do pretty much everything I need to do.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我有电脑和 FaceTime，我可以用它与家人交谈，”她解释道。她还有一台 iPad 和一部智能手机。 “所以我几乎做了我需要做的一切。”

paragraphs.sourceText: To be fair, if Rodriguez had wanted feedback from some more technophobic (害怕技术的) seniors, he might have ended up in the wrong Brookdale community. This one is located in the heart of Southern California’s aerospace corridor. Many residents have backgrounds in engineering, business and academic circles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 公平地说，如果罗德里格斯想要从一些更害怕技术的前辈那里得到反馈，他可能会进入错误的布鲁克代尔社区。该项目位于南加州航空航天走廊的中心地带。许多居民拥有工程、商业和学术界背景。

paragraphs.sourceText: But Rodriguez says he's still learning something important by moving into this Brookdale community: “People are more tech-proficient than we thought.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 但罗德里格斯表示，通过搬入布鲁克代尔社区，他仍在学习一些重要的东西：“人们比我们想象的更精通技术。”

paragraphs.sourceText: And besides, where else would he learn to play mahjong?
paragraphs.translationZh: 再说了，他还能去哪里学打麻将呢？
